headline: Lanai Planning Commission

meeting.summary: The Lānaʻi Planning Commission voted to start a parking code change and heard legal limits on proposed commissioner talk-story sessions.
meeting.recap: The commission held a public hearing on starting a parking code change for part of Lānaʻi City.[[0:03:02]] One testifier spoke in strong support of the change.[[0:04:07]] A county planner said this vote would only start the code change process.[[0:05:57]] The planner said a formal amendment is tentatively set to return on December 18th.[[0:06:19]] Commissioners voted unanimously by a show of hands to start the code change.[[0:09:41]] The chair proposed informal "talk story" sessions where commissioners discuss island topics.[[0:11:19]] The county's lawyer said the commission is always bound by the Sunshine Law, the open-meetings law.[[0:13:20]] The lawyer said everything must be on a public agenda and open to public testimony.[[0:15:47]] The vice chair said the item will likely be deferred until leaders meet with staff about agenda wording.[[0:49:57]] A testifier said a water meeting for Lānaʻi is set for December 16th.[[0:50:36]] Staff reported completed approvals for maintenance work at a beach park, including removing three dead monkeypod trees.[[0:56:27]] Staff said there are no new applicants for a commission vacancy.[[1:03:35]] The planning department plans a Lānaʻi site visit on January 18th to prepare for in-person meetings.[[1:04:32]] The next meeting is December 18 at 5:00.[[1:07:45]]
meeting.next: The planner said that if the commission moves the amendment forward, he will take it to the council. The county's lawyer said she will check with another county attorney about whether the law changed and report back. The next agenda will include a presentation by the Maui Emergency Management Agency. The chair said he will speak with one person who might be interested in the commission vacancy.

moments.q: Vote to start the parking code change
"nothing can be discussed ever between you all without it being public"
The county's lawyer reads the commission's scope of authority
The chair explains the December water commission meeting
